title: P6-08: Threat Intelligence: create the CMS app in papyrus-production (domain-free), GitHub App, repairs, first builds
description:
## Goal
Google sign-in works against the new TI pool using the EXISTING TI Google client (project 778847915037), the editors have access, and legacy sign-in is untouched.

## Context (FACT)
- Same approach as Pilobol.us P6-03: add the new Cognito domain's JavaScript origin `https://papyrus-threat-intelligence-cms.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com` and redirect URI `https://papyrus-threat-intelligence-cms.auth.us-east-1.amazoncognito.com/oauth2/idpresponse` to the same client; keep the `papyrus-threat-intelligence` entries until the retire ticket; hostnames never appear in Google. Count the entries against the 10-unverified-domain limit first (the old pool lAtce7ZTu hex b1f1d3a11a4545ba5318 is a candidate to remove, Ryan's call).
- Legacy pool t1A6sJX55 has 1 user (external provider, admin group). The earlier assessment said 2 editors are still to be named by Ryan; users do not move: each person signs in with Google once, then `admin-add-user-to-group` puts them in admin or editor of the NEW pool.
- SSM path in production: /amplify/<newTiAppId>/main-branch-<first 10 hex of sha512(appId + branch)>/GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID and GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET.

## Exact steps
1. Ryan: add the two entries on the client.
2. Pipe-copy the two SSM values legacy -> production (never printed); verify the project number prefix without printing the id.
3. Rebuild main (IdP config pushed on deploy); verify callbacks and IdP with `describe-user-pool-client`.
4. Ryan signs in at the default URL; groups assigned; the named editors sign in and are added; a non-editor test account is denied the newsroom.

## Acceptance checks
- Sign-in lands on /newsroom, groups correct, legacy https://threat-intelligence.anth.us/newsroom sign-in still works.

## Rollback
Remove the two Google entries; delete the production SSM parameters.

## Needs Ryan
Google console edits, sign-ins, the two editors' identities (never written into the repo).

## Common rules (Phase 6, PPY-7d8cd0)
- Read ~/Projects/Papyrus/AGENTS.local.md first. Assert the account with `aws sts get-caller-identity --query Account --output text` before EVERY call: profile legacy = 335163751677, profile papyrus-production = 712236451410. Never use papyrus-development; papyrus-staging (494166748521) is not used by this phase.
- Every write needs Ryan's explicit yes in chat for that step. Legacy is READ-ONLY except the steps this ticket names (each with a yes). No SCPs on legacy; never risk legacy access; no `cdk deploy` and no `ampx` against the legacy stacks of these sites.
- Never print secret values (names only; SSM values move by pipe, never to the terminal or a ticket). Ryan deletes retired resources. Do not touch Anth.us production d2hbn1ig6nqyhy or the other anth.us apps (apricity d2n7w4kwqyfwn4, babulus d3epcqvzbxdaq, tactus dfkbdffs2viq8, primus divicqm3nhcwt).
- Baselines and scratch live under ~/Projects/.baselines/phase6-<date>/ (outside any repo); clones go under ~/Projects/ and are deleted afterwards (disk is tight). Only kbs writes in the Papyrus checkout (never git add/commit there); never `git stash`.
- The committed infra/site.json in each site repo still describes the LEGACY stack until the cutover ticket; production deploys use an out-of-repo, domain-free copy (as PPY-aa93b3 did for p.apyr.us).
